name: Russian
modelReview: artifacts written 2026-11-19 by Claude Fable 5.2: a rule book (answers.md), the lexicon and hand-written rows (87 visible, 153 held out, about 330 hard cases, option rows for every style field), derived from usage notes written in Russian by a writer who knew nothing of cron. The language is written to the standard of Russian as it is written in Ukraine (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-19); the notes found no difference in the language of schedules between Ukraine and the Russian Federation and none was invented. No renderer exists yet. The author worked out the fire times of every row and re-read each sentence once; nothing has been read by a blind reader, no schedule read or fluency read by another agent has been made, and no native speaker has seen any of it. Web searches made for the forms that are the rule book's own (minutes named inside the hour, «по чётным часам», «и так каждые N часов», the six months of a two-month step) found little or nothing either way; the answers record each as a judgment to be tested; 2026-11-19, revised after two independent reads (a blind judge briefed only in Russian, 117 sentences; an adversarial schedule read of all 634 rows, which found no row whose literal content contradicts its pattern): no «кроме» on either side of a date-or-weekday union; a date over several months is each calendar date named; no parity of hours and no «и так каждые N часов» (up to four windows, else the hours as clock times and «каждого такого часа»); minutes and seconds inside their unit are ordinals with «по» and «начало»; «ежегодно» after any run of years; «того же месяца» for a nearest weekday that could cross a month's end; the 12-hour clock keeps 0:00 and writes «9 часов утра»; «ежедневно» only before a clock time. About 260 rows were rewritten by hand; the new forms («каждого такого часа», «и далее … того же часа», «весь год, кроме …», «ежедневно, а 15-го числа только по пятницам») have had no blind read; 2026-11-19, third pass, after a second blind judge read 81 changed sentences: «и далее … того же часа» and «каждого такого часа» are gone; every second hour under a finer field is «в чётные часы», «в нечётные часы» (the orchestrator's call, resting on two blind reads and no corpus source, with the ordinal count of hours a recorded risk); other hours are named as windows; seconds follow one scheme (clock times, or ordinals after «каждый раз» or of «первой минуты»); every day with one day conditional is «ежедневно, а … только …»; leading months close a union with a colon; four calendar dates or more take one «числа» over the months' names; a schedule that never fires names the month and the date it lacks. About 120 more rows were rewritten by hand and the rule book was rewritten for the builder; none of these last forms has been read by anyone but the author
